newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot resids mostly steady again, trade thin.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot resids mostly steady again, trade thin.

text.p: U.S. spot residual fuel prices mostly were unchanged again Wednesday in thin trade, with some high sulphur exports and expected interest from Florida underpinning the complex despite slack utility demand.

"I think we've seen some high sulphur demand from Mexico and some perceived demand for Florida that's helping (to keep prices up), but it's cooler than normal and there's still no actual demand," said one cash trader.
New York Harbor high sulphurs held fairly steady, with 2.2 percent still talked at about $15 a barrel, but some saw selling ahead amid talk of cargoes headed here from Europe.
NYH physical one percent also was unchanged at $16.25-50, with June paper talked closer to $16.75, traders said.
NYH 0.3 percent high pour remained talked in the $16.75-17.00 area.
At the U.S. Gulf, one percent again inched up slightly to $15.65-90 on some expected demand soon from Florida. USG three percent was little changed at $14.75-15.00.
No NYH or USG deals were reported.

New York city gate swing gas prices held relatively steady Wednesday at about $2.45/mmBtu, or $15.44 a barrel equivalent. Gas at Henry Hub, the NYMEX delivery point, also was little changed at about $2.21/mmBtu, or $13.92 a barrel.
